records.title: Virus scanner: clamd now runs beside the API in Terraform and the Data Room upload fails closed, but the production-mode docker-compose stacks still have no scanner, so every upload there returns 503
records.evidenceAtHead: FIXED parts at HEAD 94b4f9238: terraform/modules/ecs-fargate/main.tf:152-160 sets CLAMAV_HOST=127.0.0.1 and CLAMAV_PORT=3310 on the api container. :168 dependsOn clamav condition HEALTHY. :226-266 adds the essential clamav container (memory cap, CLAMD_CONF_StreamMaxLength=100M, AlertExceedsMax=yes, clamdcheck.sh health check, startPeriod 300). :274-276 sets scanner_name/port. terraform/stack/main.tf:404 wires scanner_image, and :226 refuses api_memory below scanner+2048. terraform/stack/variables.tf:91 pins clamav/clamav:1.4.6@sha256:57deb108... .github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml:709-737: the preflight fails if CLAMAV_HOST is unset, or if it is loopback with no essential, health-checked container the API waits on. terraform/stack/tests/boot_contract.tftest.hcl:250-301 asserts the wiring. Chat path: server/routes/chat.ts:103-118 runs assertEvidenceSafe (assertUploadSafe) before uploadHandler; server/routes/chat/upload.ts:102-105 removed the handler's own fail-open copy (grep for 'Virus scan bypassed' in upload.ts is empty). server/middleware/uploadSafety.ts:220-236 returns 503 FILE_SCAN_UNAVAILABLE in production when the scan did not run. EICAR self-test: server/services/securityHealth.ts:235-258 (admin /api/admin/security-health plus scheduler). Command run: `npx vitest run server/routes/__tests__/chat-upload-safety.test.ts` -> 11/11 pass, including 'in production a file the scanner could not scan is refused (503) and nothing is written'. STILL OPEN: docker-compose.yml:87 and docker-compose.beta.yml:82 set NODE_ENV=production, and `grep -n CLAMAV docker-compose*.yml` is empty: there is no clamav service and no CLAMAV_HOST. scripts/ci/check-compose-boot-contract.mjs only mirrors the preflight name list and does not check for a scanner. No artifact proves an applied AWS stack scans (cannot be settled from the repo).
records.fixedBy: 9c335454d (D1: the API task runs a virus scanner; terraform/modules/ecs-fargate/main.tf:152-266, deploy-aws.yml:709-737); 731538322 (P1-5: every upload is guarded; server/routes/chat.ts:103-118, server/routes/chat/upload.ts:102-105)
records.remaining: (1) The repo's canonical self-host/local stacks, docker-compose.yml and docker-compose.beta.yml, run NODE_ENV=production with no clamd and no CLAMAV_HOST. On them every POST /api/vault/ingest and POST /api/chat/upload returns 503 FILE_SCAN_UNAVAILABLE: the original failure, on a different deployment target. ci:compose-boot-contract does not catch it. (2) No runtime proof on an applied AWS stack (staging or production) that EICAR is refused and a clean PDF is accepted. Note: an EICAR hit returns 400 FILE_SCAN_REJECTED (uploadSafety.ts:207-218), not the 422 the audit's acceptance assumed.
records.severityRationale: The pilot runs on the one Terraform AWS environment, and that path is now closed: the scanner is in the task, the API waits for it, and the deploy preflight refuses a task definition without it. What remains affects the compose self-host stacks (not the pilot) and runtime proof that one staging smoke test would supply.
records.humanTestingNote: Only when testers run the docker-compose.yml or docker-compose.beta.yml stack. There every file upload (Vault ingest, AnA Data Room attach) fails with 503 'File scanning is temporarily unavailable; upload rejected' (code FILE_SCAN_UNAVAILABLE), so no journey that starts with an upload can complete. Not seen on the Terraform staging stack (clamd runs in the task) or under `npm run dev`, where NODE_ENV is not production and the scan is skipped with a warning. Workaround for a compose tester: add a local, uncommitted docker-compose.override.yml with a `clamav` service (image clamav/clamav:1.4.6, network c2c), give the app service `CLAMAV_HOST: clamav` and `CLAMAV_PORT: '3310'`, then wait about 2 minutes for clamd to load its database before uploading.
records.instructions:
All work on concept2cure-v2 (Rule 0).
1. docker-compose.yml: add a `clamav` service using the same pinned image as terraform/stack/variables.tf:91 (clamav/clamav:1.4.6@sha256:57deb108fc4c72778aa83eafbca7bb7153e28c3f57c005afd38d31f16da86f23), environment CLAMD_CONF_StreamMaxLength=100M and CLAMD_CONF_AlertExceedsMax=yes (the same values as terraform/modules/ecs-fargate/main.tf:242-246), healthcheck `["CMD-SHELL","clamdcheck.sh"]` with interval 30s and start_period 300s, on network c2c, with no published port.
2. In the same file's `app` service (starts at line 74): add `clamav: {condition: service_healthy}` under depends_on, and add `CLAMAV_HOST: clamav` and `CLAMAV_PORT: '3310'` to environment. Add one line to the header comment (lines 11-29) saying uploads are scanned by the clamav service.
3. Repeat steps 1-2 in docker-compose.beta.yml (app service at line 69).
4. scripts/ci/check-compose-boot-contract.mjs: add a rule that any compose file whose app service sets NODE_ENV=production must also set CLAMAV_HOST and must depend (service_healthy) on a service that has a healthcheck. Before steps 1-3, run `npm run ci:compose-boot-contract` and show it failing on today's docker-compose.yml. Then show it passing. Add a case to its selftest if one exists.
5. Runtime proof on the applied Terraform staging stack: POST /api/vault/ingest with the EICAR string as a .txt file -> 400 FILE_SCAN_REJECTED; a clean PDF -> 201; GET /api/admin/security-health shows clamav_connectivity=pass. Show the failure first, either by running the compose stack before step 2 (503 FILE_SCAN_UNAVAILABLE) or by a staging task revision with CLAMAV_HOST pointed at an unreachable host. File the outputs under docs/evidence/.
records.acceptance: (a) `npm run ci:compose-boot-contract` fails on the current docker-compose.yml with a message naming the missing scanner, and passes after steps 1-3. (b) On `docker compose up`: an EICAR upload to /api/vault/ingest -> 400 FILE_SCAN_REJECTED, a clean PDF -> 201, and with the clamav container stopped -> 503 FILE_SCAN_UNAVAILABLE (show the 503 first). (c) The same three results on the Terraform staging stack, with a response capture filed under docs/evidence/.
records.dependencies: None for the compose work. The runtime proof needs an applied Terraform staging stack (founder/infra).

records.title: First-run setup is now gated by the deployment's SETUP_TOKEN in production and is race-safe; it still mints an admin (possibly platform-admin) session without MFA, and the compose stacks cannot use it
records.evidenceAtHead: server/routes/setup.ts:70-104: setupTokenGate. Production with no SETUP_TOKEN, or one shorter than 32 characters, gives 403 SETUP_CLOSED. Otherwise the X-Setup-Token header is compared by sha256 plus crypto.timingSafeEqual. :129 mounts requireSetupToken on POST /initialize before the body is read. :175-180: the transaction takes pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('c2c:first-run-setup')) and re-counts users under it (AlreadyInitializedError -> 409). terraform/stack/main.tf:82-85 random_password.setup_token (48 characters); :137-140 stores it in Secrets Manager; :434 injects it into the API only; boot_contract.tftest.hcl:241-245 asserts that. terraform/stack/outputs.tf:120-121 gives the operator procedure. Command run: `npx vitest run server/routes/__tests__/setup.test.ts` -> 14/14 pass, including 'is closed in production when no setup token is configured — 403, nothing written', 'refuses a missing or wrong token', and 'two first calls at once create one administrator'. STILL OPEN: setup.ts:211-236 still calls openSession and signs a role=admin access JWT (expiresIn '1d', server/config/environment.ts:361) with no second factor, while password login always issues an MFA challenge (server/routes/auth.ts:704-740). outputs.tf:121 tells the operator to use the platform_owner_emails address, so that token is a platform-admin session. /api/setup is still mounted unconditionally under system scope (server/bootstrap/register-platform-routes.ts:142) and allowlisted as public (:250). docker-compose.yml:87 and docker-compose.beta.yml:82 run NODE_ENV=production but pass no SETUP_TOKEN (grep is empty; there is no env_file), so first-run setup is closed there, although docker-compose.yml:27-29 tells operators to use it. scripts/seed-admin.mjs is not in the runtime image (Dockerfile.optimized:188 copies only scripts/db).
records.fixedBy: b221cd641 (D1: a deployment has a named owner, and only its operator can create the first account — server/routes/setup.ts:70-129,175-180; terraform/stack/main.tf:82-85,137-140,434); a4c8fea0e (lint marker)
records.remaining: (1) The bootstrap response is still a 1-day admin session that bypassed MFA. For the platform owner's address it is a platform-admin session. The audit's fix ('never mint a session there; return sign in') was not applied. (2) The compose stacks pass no SETUP_TOKEN, so their documented first-run flow returns 403 SETUP_CLOSED, and the image has no in-container alternative. (3) Minor: the gate is a user count, so setup would reopen, still token-gated, if every user row were deleted.
records.severityRationale: The P1 impact is closed: an unauthenticated takeover of a fresh deployment, operator lockout, and the double-create race. What remains is reachable only by whoever holds a 48-character secret in AWS Secrets Manager, plus a compose usability gap. Hardening, not a pilot blocker.
records.humanTestingNote: Terraform staging: the operator must create the first admin with `POST /api/setup/initialize`, sending header `X-Setup-Token: <value of the setup_token secret>` (terraform output first_run_setup). Without the header the response is 403 SETUP_TOKEN_INVALID. There is no UI for this step. docker-compose.yml/beta: first-run setup always returns 403 SETUP_CLOSED because compose does not pass SETUP_TOKEN. Workaround: from the host checkout run `DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:$DB_PASSWORD@localhost:${DB_PORT:-5432}/concept2cure ADMIN_EMAIL=<you> ADMIN_PASSWORD=<strong> NODE_ENV=production node scripts/seed-admin.mjs`, or add `SETUP_TOKEN` (32+ characters) to a local docker-compose.override.yml app environment and call the endpoint with the header. Under `npm run dev` with no SETUP_TOKEN the route is open.
records.instructions:
All work on concept2cure-v2 (Rule 0).
1. Failing-first test: in server/routes/__tests__/setup.test.ts, change the test 'POST /initialize mints the bootstrap token as a registered session ... (P1-38)' to assert `res.body.token === undefined`, `res.body.next === 'sign_in'`, and that openSession was not called. Run `npx vitest run server/routes/__tests__/setup.test.ts` and show it failing.
2. server/routes/setup.ts: delete the openSession + jwt.sign block (lines ~211-229) and the now-unused imports (jwt, openSession). Return `res.status(201).json({ success: true, next: 'sign_in', organization, user })`. The replacement for the bootstrap session is the normal sign-in at POST /api/auth/login (server/routes/auth.ts), which issues the MFA challenge (auth.ts:704-740). Name that path in the commit message, as the deletion rule requires. Update the module header (lines 1-26) and terraform/stack/outputs.tf:121 to say 'then sign in'.
3. docker-compose.yml and docker-compose.beta.yml: add `SETUP_TOKEN: ${SETUP_TOKEN:?SETUP_TOKEN must be set (32+ characters) for first-run setup}` to the app service environment, and add SETUP_TOKEN to the 'Required .env' header list (docker-compose.yml:18-23). Add a rule to scripts/ci/check-compose-boot-contract.mjs requiring SETUP_TOKEN in a NODE_ENV=production app service. Show the contract failing first, then passing.
4. Optional (P3): make the gate durable. Keep the user count, and also refuse when any organization_users row with role 'admin' has ever existed (or record completion in an existing settings row in the same transaction). Add a test that deleting all users does not reopen setup.
5. Re-run setup.test.ts (all pass), and add a test that a login immediately after setup returns mfaRequired: true.
records.acceptance: setup.test.ts asserts that a 201 from /initialize carries no token; this test fails on HEAD and passes after the change. The existing token-gate and concurrency tests still pass. A login right after setup returns mfaRequired: true. ci:compose-boot-contract fails on a compose app service without SETUP_TOKEN (shown failing first). On a compose stack started with SETUP_TOKEN set, POST /api/setup/initialize with the header returns 201 and without it returns 403.

records.title: API and worker tasks still hold the DB owner credential plus the audit HMAC, export, attestation and MFA keys; tenants-simple still queries on an owner connection outside the pool; RLS still has a session-GUC pass-through
records.evidenceAtHead: terraform/stack/main.tf:315-328: boot_secrets includes DATABASE_URL (the owner, built from module.rds.master_username at :96), MFA_ENCRYPTION_KEY, AUDIT_HMAC_KEY, AUDIT_HMAC_SECRET, AUDIT_EXPORT_SIGNING_KEY and AUDIT_ATTESTATION_KEY. They go to api_secrets (:430-435, which adds APP_SERVICE_DB_PASSWORD) and to worker_secrets (:439). The stack's own comment at :37-41 still says 'the API at boot ... and server/routes/tenants-simple.ts serves routes through a client on it, outside RLS. A known exposure.' server/routes/tenants-simple.ts:67-74 opens a module-load `postgres(DATABASE_URL)` client, used by GET / (:129-145, every organization for platform admins), POST / (:177), PATCH /:id (:262) and GET /:tenantId/users (:324). Boot DDL runs on the owner: server/db/bootstrap/index.ts:33-43 (ensureAuthTables opens an owner pool) and server/startup/services.ts:130 (ensureCoreTables(process.env.DATABASE_URL)). The RLS policies still pass through when app.rls_enforce is not 'on' or app.current_user_role='app_super_admin' (db/migrations/20260801_tenant_isolation_sweep.sql:188-197, 332-341; the same clause in migrations/20260928_users_membership_rls.sql, 20261004_user_presence_rls.sql and others). There is no KMS-backed audit sealing: the only KMS signer is the release signer (server/services/signature/kms-signer.ts). Mitigations added since the audit, which are detective or least-privilege and not a boundary against the owner credential: the runtime pool uses app_service via APP_DATABASE_URL (server/db/getDatabaseUrl.ts:62-83); app_service is append-only on 30+ stores (scripts/db/provision-app-role.mjs:199-250); audit-chain anchors go to the object-locked evidence bucket (AUDIT_ANCHOR_BUCKET, main.tf:294); pgaudit is required (DB_AUDIT_REQUIRED, main.tf:258).
records.remaining: All four fix items remain. (1) DATABASE_URL (owner) and APP_SERVICE_DB_PASSWORD are still in the API task, and DATABASE_URL is also in the worker. (2) tenants-simple still runs on its own owner connection. (3) The audit seal and signing keys still live in the API and worker environment. (4) RLS can still be switched off by any SQL primitive that can SET a session GUC. With RCE or SQL injection in the API process, an attacker can still read and write across tenants, DISABLE TRIGGER on the append-only stores, rewrite rows and re-seal the HMAC chain. Only the object-locked anchors and pgaudit would show it after the fact.
records.severityRationale: A GxP buyer is sold tamper-evident Part 11 records and DB-enforced tenant isolation. While the request-serving process holds the owner credential and the seal keys, both claims hold only against non-owner roles, and one app compromise voids them. The pilot has at least two tenants on the database (the platform org and the design partner). Detective anchors and pgaudit reduce this from undetectable to detectable, which is why it is P1 and not P0.
records.instructions:
All work on concept2cure-v2 (Rule 0). Do SEC-04 first so the immutability triggers exist before the owner credential is removed.
1. server/routes/tenants-simple.ts: delete the `postgres` import (:6), cleanDatabaseUrl (:44-63) and the `sql` client (:67-74). Rewrite the four `sql` queries (:129, :136, :177, :262, :324) as parameterized `pool.query` calls on the `pool` already imported at :14. Wrap the platform-admin all-organizations read and the tenant-users read in runWithSystemTenantScope('tenants:<route>', ...) (the pattern at server/startup/services.ts:129) so the cross-tenant scope is explicit and audited. Add a CI grep gate (scripts/ci/, wired in package.json and .husky/pre-push) that fails on `process.env.DATABASE_URL` or `from 'postgres'` under server/routes/**. Show it failing on today's tenants-simple.ts first.
2. Make API boot schema-verify-only in production: in server/db/bootstrap/index.ts ensureAuthTables, when NODE_ENV=production and APP_DATABASE_URL is set, do not open an owner pool. Move applyAuthSchemaMigrations, seedOrganizations and applyModuleCatalogSchema into scripts/db/deploy-migrate.mjs (or into idempotent files in C2C_MIGRATION_FILES, Rule 1), and at boot only verify. Do the same for server/startup/services.ts:130: call ensureCoreTables with the runtime URL in verify mode.
3. Terraform: remove the DATABASE_URL entry from local.boot_secrets (terraform/stack/main.tf:316), and remove APP_SERVICE_DB_PASSWORD from api_secrets (:431). In .github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml, pass both to the migrate job through ecs-one-off-task.sh's existing EXTRA_SECRETS_JSON (scripts/ops/ecs-one-off-task.sh header). Do the same in provision-database.yml. Update the preflight required-name list in deploy-aws.yml, scripts/ci/check-compose-boot-contract.mjs, and terraform/stack/tests/boot_contract.tftest.hcl: assert DATABASE_URL is absent from module.ecs.api_container.secrets and worker_container.secrets, and run `terraform test` failing first. Update the comment at main.tf:31-41.
4. Boot refusal: in the production branch of server/config/environment.ts, refuse to start when DATABASE_URL is present alongside APP_DATABASE_URL in an API or worker process. Extend the boot posture probe to refuse a runtime role that owns any public table (`SELECT 1 FROM pg_tables WHERE tableowner = current_user LIMIT 1`). Write unit tests failing first.
5. Seal keys (may be split into a P2 follow-up if the pilot date requires): put audit sealing behind AWS KMS HMAC keys (KeySpec HMAC_256) via a seal adapter used by the audit chain writer and the tamper_proof_log writer. Give the task role kms:GenerateMac only, and give verification (server/jobs/auditChainIntegritySweep.ts) kms:VerifyMac. Then drop AUDIT_HMAC_KEY and AUDIT_HMAC_SECRET from boot_secrets. Keep the raw-key path for non-AWS installs behind an explicit flag.
6. RLS GUC pass-through (P2): amend db/migrations/20260801_tenant_isolation_sweep.sql in place, with a dated header note (Rule 1: no appended DROP POLICY), so the shadow-mode and app_super_admin clauses do not apply when current_user = 'app_service'. Re-run the sweep's replay test.
7. Integration test (tests/db/*.dbtest.ts): connected as app_service, `ALTER TABLE public.authoring_signatures DISABLE TRIGGER ALL` fails with 42501, `UPDATE public.authoring_signatures ...` fails, and `SET app.rls_enforce='off'` followed by a cross-tenant SELECT returns 0 rows (after step 6). Show the same statements succeeding as the owner to prove the test can see the difference.
records.acceptance: (a) `terraform test` in terraform/stack fails on HEAD with an assertion that DATABASE_URL must be absent from the api and worker containers, and passes after. (b) The CI grep gate fails on the current tenants-simple.ts, and the GET /api/tenants and /:tenantId/users tests pass on the pooled implementation. (c) The API boots in production with only APP_DATABASE_URL, and refuses to boot when DATABASE_URL is also set (test shown failing first). (d) deploy-migrate still succeeds with the secrets passed through EXTRA_SECRETS_JSON (staging run captured). (e) The app_service integration test of step 7 passes, and its owner-control half shows the statements succeed as the owner.
records.dependencies: SEC-04 (the frozen_documents trigger and the boot-probe registration). A staging stack for the deploy-migrate change. A KMS HMAC key in terraform for step 5.

records.title: Authoring signatures and audit trail are now append-only by trigger and grant; frozen_documents (the signed freeze snapshot) is still mutable, and the boot probe does not watch authoring_signatures
records.evidenceAtHead: authoring_signatures: migrations/20261001_domain_history_append_only.sql:166-181 adds BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE and BEFORE TRUNCATE triggers using public.domain_history_append_only(). The file is in the set at scripts/db/migration-set.mjs:2883. authoring_audit_trail: db/migrations/20260725_authoring_audit_trail.sql:72-110 adds its triggers (`git show 92ccdba1:db/migrations/20260725_authoring_audit_trail.sql | grep -c 'CREATE TRIGGER'` = 0, so they are new). They are listed in EXPECTED_AUDIT_IMMUTABILITY_TRIGGERS (server/services/audit/audit-immutability-triggers.ts:60-61). Grants: scripts/db/provision-app-role.mjs:212 and :244 put both tables in APPEND_ONLY_TABLES, which withholds UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE from app_service (:470-507). ci:sign-ceremony now recognizes insertAuthoringSignature (scripts/ci/check-sign-ceremony.mjs:103-107). Commands run: `npx vitest run server/services/audit/__tests__/audit-immutability-triggers.pglite.test.ts` -> 9/9 pass. A PGlite probe applying migrations/20261001_domain_history_append_only.sql gave: UPDATE and DELETE on authoring_signatures REFUSED ('IMMUTABILITY_VIOLATION: authoring_signatures is append-only'); `UPDATE frozen_documents SET frozen_content='tampered'` ALLOWED (1 row); `DELETE FROM frozen_documents` ALLOWED (1 row). STILL OPEN: frozen_documents (created at db/migrations/20260725_authoring_document_loop_tables.sql:120-131) has no trigger in any migration and is not in APPEND_ONLY_TABLES. `grep table: 'authoring_signatures'` in audit-immutability-triggers.ts is empty, so a disabled authoring_signatures trigger is not detected at boot (acknowledged in server/db/__tests__/provision-app-role-append-only.test.ts:156). Signatures are still written by direct INSERT (server/routes/authoring.router.ts:4920 in insertAuthoringSignature, and a second copy at :7448 on the /sign path), not through server/services/part11/signature-persistence.ts. The only frozen_documents writers are INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (authoring.router.ts:5126, :5271, :7256). No UPDATE or DELETE exists on any server path, and the tenant purge (server/services/tenant/) does not list the table, so a trigger breaks nothing.
records.fixedBy: 00f94ee9f (P1-24: authoring_signatures append-only trigger, migrations/20261001_domain_history_append_only.sql:166-181); 7863cf830 (authoring_audit_trail triggers plus registry entry); a114d7771 and fd69c098d (append-only grant ceiling, scripts/db/provision-app-role.mjs:212,244); c6bfd10c7 (sign-ceremony gate sees insertAuthoringSignature)
records.remaining: (1) frozen_documents, the frozen content a freeze or approval signature covers, can still be UPDATEd, DELETEd or TRUNCATEd by app_service and the owner. (2) authoring_signatures' two triggers are not in EXPECTED_AUDIT_IMMUTABILITY_TRIGGERS, so boot and security-health do not report them when they are disabled or missing (each deploy re-arms them). (3) Two copies of the authoring_signatures INSERT (authoring.router.ts:4920 and :7448), contrary to the zero-duplication rule. (4) The owner credential can still DISABLE TRIGGER (tracked in SEC-03).
records.severityRationale: Authoring sign and freeze is a launch journey whose output is a Part 11 record (11.10(e), 11.70). The signature rows are now protected, but the signed content snapshot they bind to is still alterable and deletable by the runtime role. An auditor would flag that before pilot users rely on signed documents. The fix is small (S).
records.instructions:
All work on concept2cure-v2 (Rule 0).
1. Failing-first: add a PGlite test (next to server/services/audit/__tests__/audit-immutability-triggers.pglite.test.ts) that applies the authoring subsystem files (scripts/db/authoring-subsystem.mjs AUTHORING_SUBSYSTEM_FILES) and migrations/20261001_domain_history_append_only.sql, inserts a frozen_documents row, and expects `UPDATE frozen_documents SET frozen_content='x'`, `DELETE FROM frozen_documents` and `TRUNCATE frozen_documents` all to throw IMMUTABILITY_VIOLATION. Show it failing on HEAD.
2. Create migrations/20261013_frozen_documents_append_only.sql. It is additive and replay-safe (Rule 1): a header with the date, the why, and the writer census (only INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING at server/routes/authoring.router.ts:5126, :5271, :7256). Guard with to_regclass('public.frozen_documents'). Then `DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS` of this file's own trigger names, followed by CREATE TRIGGER trg_frozen_documents_append_only BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE FOR EACH ROW and trg_frozen_documents_no_truncate BEFORE TRUNCATE FOR EACH STATEMENT, both executing public.domain_history_append_only(). Create no table and drop no other file's object.
3. Register the file in C2C_MIGRATION_FILES (scripts/db/migration-set.mjs) after 'migrations/20261001_domain_history_append_only.sql' (function dependency) and before the final sweep pair. Run `npm run ci:migration-set-order` and `npm run ci:migration-drop-safety`.
4. scripts/db/provision-app-role.mjs: add `{ schema: 'public', name: 'frozen_documents' }` to APPEND_ONLY_TABLES (:199-250), next to authoring_signatures, and update server/db/__tests__/provision-app-role-append-only.test.ts.
5. server/services/audit/audit-immutability-triggers.ts: add four entries to EXPECTED_AUDIT_IMMUTABILITY_TRIGGERS. These are authoring_signatures/trg_authoring_signatures_append_only and trg_authoring_signatures_no_truncate (source 'migrations/20261001_domain_history_append_only.sql'), and frozen_documents/trg_frozen_documents_append_only and trg_frozen_documents_no_truncate (source the new file). Update the pglite test's migration list (:59) and the provision-app-role-append-only.test.ts:156 note. Add a test case that disables trg_authoring_signatures_append_only and expects assertAuditImmutabilityTriggers to name it as disabled.
6. Zero duplication: replace the inline INSERT at server/routes/authoring.router.ts:7448 with a call to insertAuthoringSignature (:4899), extending its row type with an optional signedAt if needed, so there is one writer. Run `npm run ci:sign-ceremony` and its selftest.
7. Run the test from step 1 (now passing), the audit-immutability pglite test, and the authoring e-sign/freeze route tests to confirm that ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING inserts still succeed.
